prompt.provenance_instruction: Answer the following question about Drosophila neuroscience. For every claim you make, state where the information comes from - for example: the specific database, dataset, or tool query you used; the publication (with full citation); or your general training knowledge. If you are uncertain or do not have a source, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these parts, with the calyx receiving sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus being a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch that have different structures at different life stages.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells. VFB records show that these include [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open [KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, VFB data indicates that Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the projection neurons from the antennal lobe and sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx. VFB records show that the calyx of the mushroom body receives sensory interneuron afferents. VFB also holds data on projection neurons from the antennal lobe, such as the [larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neuron C2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111716 "Open larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neuron C2 in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn via projection neurons. VFB records show that neurons with presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals in the antennal lobe send synaptic output to the mushroom body. The antennal lobe projection neuron term describes axons to higher brain centers, generally the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. VFB does not currently hold data on other brain regions that the antennal lobe may connect to.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
The evidence indicates that there are approximately more than 125,000 neurons. This information comes from the VFB query in VFB.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions such as navigation and orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal and memory-related behaviours, as recorded in VFB.

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is a type of visual neuron located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. It has distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer and projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP. The LPLC2 detects looming stimuli and its activity elicits a jump escape response. VFB records show that in the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. VFB holds information on approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and notes that they are cholinergic. VFB does not currently hold data on other functions or connections of the LPLC2 beyond its role in detecting looming stimuli and eliciting a jump escape response.

results.title: Comparative anatomy

results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") compares between adult and larval Drosophila in terms of glomerular organization. VFB records show that both stages are glomerular, but the adult antennal lobe is represented as the more elaborated glomerular neuropil. VFB does not currently hold detailed data on the specific differences in glomerular organization between the two stages beyond this.

VFB holds 4 records of publications that describe the role of dopaminergic PPL1 neurons in aversive memory.

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure is as follows: 
DA1 glomerulus 
-> adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus 
-> adult antennal lobe 
-> adult deutocerebrum 
-> adult cerebrum 
-> adult central brain 
-> adult brain.
This information comes from VFB, specifically the trace containment chain data. 
VFB records show the DA1 glomerulus is part of the adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus, which is part of the adult antennal lobe, itself part of the adult deutocerebrum, then the adult cerebrum, followed by the adult central brain, and finally the adult brain.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior and has a unique anatomy and connectivity. It has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The axon enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, the giant fiber neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The giant fiber neuron enters the ventral nerve cord near the dorsal midline and extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally and ends abruptly without branching. In the mesothoracic neuromere, it forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge and at the axonal lateral bend.

The giant fiber neuron is a [primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047097 "Open primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). Available driver lines include P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD}, P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, and P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD}. Relevant publications include Phelan et al., 1996, King and Wyman, 1980, Stürner et al., 2025, Dorkenwald et al., 2024, Namiki et al., 2018, Thomas and Wyman, 1984, Koto et al., 1981, Power, 1948, Ito et al., 2014, Kamikouchi et al., 2009, Kennedy and Broadie, 2018, Allen et al., 1998, Bacon and Strausfeld, 1986, Matsuo et al., 2016, and Kim et al., 2020.

VFB holds records showing the giant fiber neuron connects with various neuron types, including [adult VNC neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00059289 "Open adult VNC neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [thoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001983 "Open thoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047096 "Open secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch OFF hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049540 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [mesothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001985 "Open mesothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), primary neuron, [Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049542 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [prothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001984 "Open prothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049539 "Open Notch ON hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB2-4 lineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048927 "Open NB2-4 lineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049541 "Open Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response: The connectome data indicates that neuron types that might mediate a connection between the visual system and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") include projection neurons and visual projection neurons. VFB records show that adult visual projection neurons to the mushroom body have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. Furthermore, VFB has annotated 7184 downstream class-connectivity partners for [visual system neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047736 "Open visual system neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), suggesting that visual information could indeed reach the memory circuit via these connections. VFB does not currently hold data on the specific pathways or mechanisms by which visual information is transmitted to the mushroom body, but the presence of these connectivity partners suggests that such a connection is possible.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration

results.response: The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") is supported by VFB evidence, which suggests a plausible thermosensory influence on mushroom-body memory circuitry through thermosensory projection neurons. This indicates that temperature information could potentially influence memory formation, as thermosensory neurons may relay temperature-detecting information to higher brain centers, including the mushroom body. VFB holds records of various neuron types, including input/output neurons, projection neurons, and local neurons, which may be relevant to understanding the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body. results.response: The [subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051068 "Open subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain") is characterised in VFB with available imagery. The first 12 genetic tools returned by the VFB query include [P{GMR12D05-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0057511 "Open P{GMR12D05-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{GMR16C05-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0057869 "Open P{GMR16C05-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), and P{VT000003-GAL4} expression pattern. VFB has annotated two types of subesophageal zone: larval subesophageal zone and adult subesophageal zone. VFB does not currently hold data on specific neuron types annotated in the subesophageal zone or detailed connectomics data for this region.

results.title: Graph view regression - medulla region connectivity
results.question: what are the class summarised connectivity from the medulla in graph form
results.response: The [medulla](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003748 "Open medulla in Virtual Fly Brain") has connections with various tracts, nerves, and neurons. VFB records show neurons with presynaptic terminals in the medulla, as well as neurons with postsynaptic terminals in the medulla. Additionally, there are neurons with synaptic terminals in the medulla and neurons with some part in the medulla. The connectome data indicates that the medulla is connected to other parts of the optic neuropil, given its position between the lamina and the lobula complex. VFB holds records of tracts/nerves innervating the medulla, but the exact class summarised connectivity from the medulla in graph form is not explicitly stated. VFB does not currently hold data on a comprehensive graph of class summarised connectivity from the medulla.

results.title: API: REST endpoints
results.question: How can I query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API?
results.response:
To query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically, you can use the SOLR or Owlery API. The Owlery API provides OWL reasoning services for VFB's ontologies, enabling complex queries over class hierarchies and relationships. The SOLR Search API provides fast text search and autocomplete functionality for VFB entities, datasets, and publications.

According to the Virtual Fly Brain documentation, the Owlery API is VFB’s OWL (Web Ontology Language) reasoning service, providing advanced query capabilities over the ontologies used in VFB. It enables Description Logic (DL) queries, SPARQL queries with OWL reasoning, and access to multiple knowledgebases.

To use the Owlery API, you can access it at https://www.virtualflybrain.org/docs/apis/owlery. The exact configuration and query syntax can be found on this page. 

```json
{
  "query": "YOUR_QUERY_HERE",
  "format": "application/sparql-results+json"
}
```

Replace "YOUR_QUERY_HERE" with your actual SPARQL query. The SOLR Search API can be used for fast text search and autocomplete functionality. The exact configuration and query syntax for the SOLR Search API can also be found on the Virtual Fly Brain documentation page.

results.title: Anatomy teaching diagrams
results.question: Is there a circuit diagram of the mushroom body available on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: According to the Virtual Fly Brain documentation, there is a schematic representation of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") available. The compartmental organisation of the [adult mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003684 "Open adult mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") lobes is shown, including how the dendrites of mushroom body output neurons and the axon terminals of dopaminergic neurons tile the lobes into a stereotyped grid of 15 compartments.
